correctness.rationale: Every connected four-vertex three-edge undirected graph is K1,3 or P4. Strict subhomogeneity of the SIS fixed-point map gives uniqueness of any positive equilibrium and hence node-orbit symmetry. Eliminating nodes yields explicit star and path equilibria and physical thresholds; with both positive, an exact positive-denominator factorization reduces the prevalence gap to ((t+1)^3-4t^3). The unique root is t=1/(2^(2/3)-1), and exact expansions establish the 1/(3t) high-rate gap. Replaying checker.py from the actual packaged file passed 60,415 assertions, including symbolic identities; sampled cases are not used to prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The two graph types exhaust the smallest equal-vertex/equal-edge connected-tree comparison with nonisomorphic choices; no artificial parameter slice is imposed. A sharp all-rate ranking and explicit high-transmission coefficient distinguish spectral-onset heuristics from endemic-burden ranking, giving a natural finite test case for network epidemiology models. The exact special-case classification and uniqueness are the useful claims, not the already known general phenomenon of some network-rank reversal.
